spans.s:
Ula is the name of some unknown wild animal, perhaps, as
Whitney^1 suggests, the ‘jackal.’ It is mentioned in the
Atharvaveda^2 and later Saṃhitās,^3 but not definitely identified
by the commentators.
1) Translation of the Atharvaveda,
669.
2) xii. 1, 49.
3) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 5, 12, 1 (as
ūla); Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 13, 12;
14, 2; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 31. Cf.
ulala in Baudhāyana Śrauta Sūtra, ii. 5.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 82.
Ūla is a variant of Ula.

Ula Vārṣṇi-vṛddha is mentioned as a teacher in the Kauṣītaki
Brāhmaṇa (vii. 4).

Ulapa^1 is the name of a species of grass referred to in the
Rigveda and the later Saṃhitās.^2
1) x. 142, 3.
2) Av. vii. 66, 1. Adjectives derived
from the word are ulapya (Vājasaneyi
Saṃhitā, xvi. 45, etc.) and upolapa
(Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, i. 7, 2).
